languageModelTools.name: bitbucket_getPullRequest
languageModelTools.displayName: Get Bitbucket Pull Request
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches a Bitbucket pull request's title, description, author, target branch, and source commit hash.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View a Bitbucket pull request's details.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetches the unified diff for a Bitbucket pull request.
languageModelTools.userDescription: View a Bitbucket pull request's diff.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

contextLines.description: Diff context lines to request around each hunk (default: the configured ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewContextLines, 12).

languageModelTools.name: bitbucket_postComment
languageModelTools.displayName: Post Bitbucket Comment
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Posts a comment to a Bitbucket pull request's activity feed. This writes to Bitbucket — the user is asked to confirm the exact comment text before it is posted.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Post a comment on a Bitbucket pull request.

project.description: Bitbucket project key (Data Center) or workspace (Cloud), e.g. PROJ or myworkspace

comment.description: The comment text to post to the pull request's activity feed.

languageModelTools.name: jira_check_connection
languageModelTools.displayName: Check the Jira connection
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks the Jira connection Ticket Sidekick uses. Reports the base URL, the auth type, whether a token is stored and the signed-in Jira user; when the setup is incomplete or wrong, says what is missing or wrong and how to fix it. Takes no input and changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Checks the Jira connection Ticket Sidekick uses.

languageModelTools.name: jira_view_ticket
languageModelTools.displayName: View a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shows one Jira ticket in full: the fields chosen by the Ticket Sidekick display settings, the whole description, the attachments (name, size and type) and the comments, newest first, up to 100, with a note when older ones are left out. Without ticketKey, uses the ticket key in the current git branch of the first workspace folder and says which folder and branch it used, or that the branch holds no key. Changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Shows one Jira ticket in full.

ticketKey.description: The ticket key, e.g. PROJ-123. Leave it out to use the key in the current git branch.

languageModelTools.name: jira_find_tickets
languageModelTools.displayName: Find Jira tickets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Finds Jira tickets by JQL or by a saved filter (id or name); give exactly one of jql and filter. Use it for your own lookups and to answer a question about tickets. When the user asks to see a list of tickets, or to change more than one ticket, call jira_open_board with board ticket-list instead and do not list the tickets in chat. When the request matches one of the user's saved filters (see jira_list_my_filters), use that filter rather than writing new JQL. "My team" means the team JQL in the ticketSidekick.jira.myTeamJql setting: set myTeam to true to narrow by it instead of guessing who is on the team. Narrow further with fixVersion, sprint and assignee ("me" for the signed-in user). Shows 50 tickets per page with the columns from the ticketSidekick.jira.searchFields setting; when more tickets match, the answer gives the page value for the next call. Changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Finds Jira tickets by JQL or by a saved filter (id or name); give exactly one of jql and filter.

jql.description: A JQL query. Give either jql or filter.

filter.description: A saved filter, by its id or its name. Give either jql or filter.

fixVersion.description: Narrow to a fix version, by name; resolved in the single project the query scopes to.

sprint.description: Narrow to a sprint, by name; resolved in the single project the query scopes to.

assignee.description: Narrow to an assignee: a user name, or "me" for the signed-in user.

myTeam.description: Narrow by the team JQL from the ticketSidekick.jira.myTeamJql setting ("my team").

page.description: The page value a previous answer gave, to read the next page of the same query.

languageModelTools.name: jira_list_my_filters
languageModelTools.displayName: List my Jira filters
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the user's saved Jira filters, favourites and owned ones, each once, with name and id. Pass a filter's id or name to jira_find_tickets to run it. Takes no input and changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists the user's saved Jira filters, favourites and owned ones, each once, with name and id.

languageModelTools.name: jira_workflow
languageModelTools.displayName: Show the statuses a Jira ticket can reach
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the statuses a Jira ticket can be moved to from its current status, each with the transitions that lead there, from the workflow of the ticket's project and issue type cached in the workspace. When no workflow is cached yet, it is discovered from Jira by sampling tickets and saved to the cache; refresh: true discovers it again. Changes nothing in Jira; it only writes the local cache file.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists the statuses a Jira ticket can be moved to from its current status, each with the transitions that lead there, from the workflow of the ticket's project and issue type cached in the workspace.

refresh.description: Discover the workflow from Jira again and rewrite the cache, even when one is cached.

languageModelTools.name: jira_list_templates
languageModelTools.displayName: List the Jira ticket templates
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the ticket templates defined in the workspace's .jira-templates.json: each template's name, its issue type, the default field values it sets, the fields it looks up when a ticket is created, and its description sections. Takes no input and changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists the ticket templates defined in the workspace's .jira-templates.json.

languageModelTools.name: jira_create_template
languageModelTools.displayName: Create a ticket template from a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Saves a new ticket template to the workspace's .jira-templates.json, built from one reference ticket: its issue type and the values of its template fields (priority, labels, components, sprint, team). Fields that are empty on the ticket are left out. When a template with that name exists, the new one is saved as "<name> (2)", "<name> (3)" and so on; no template is replaced. Ask the user for the name before calling. The same template within a minute is skipped.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Saves a new ticket template to the workspace's .jira-templates.json, built from one reference ticket.

ticketKey.description: The reference ticket, e.g. PROJ-123. Its issue type and its template fields (priority, labels, components, sprint, team) are copied.

name.description: The name of the new template, as the user gave it.

languageModelTools.name: jira_load_ticket
languageModelTools.displayName: Load a Jira ticket into the workspace
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Use when the user asks to load or download a ticket, e.g. "load PROJ-123". Downloads one Jira ticket into `.jira-context/<KEY>/` in the first workspace folder, so its content can be read as local files: `ticket.md` (fields, description, web links, attachment list), `comments.md` (all comments) and, in `attachments/`, the text, image, document and archive attachments. Binary attachments of other types are skipped unless named in attachments; files over 100 MB are always skipped. The answer lists every file written by its absolute path and every skipped attachment with its size and the reason. Without ticketKey, uses the ticket key in the current git branch of the first workspace folder and says which folder and branch it used. Changes nothing in Jira; it only writes local files, overwriting an earlier load.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Use when the user asks to load or download a ticket, e.g.

ticketKey.description: The ticket key, e.g. PROJ-123. Leave it out to use the key in the current git branch.

attachments.description: Attachment filenames to download as well, exactly as the ticket lists them, including ones the default filter skips (such as binary files). Files over 100 MB are never downloaded.

languageModelTools.name: jira_move_ticket
languageModelTools.displayName: Move a Jira ticket to another status
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Moves one Jira ticket to a target status, in one transition or along several when the workflow needs them. To move several tickets, call jira_open_board with board ticket-list and the move as change; do not call this once per ticket. When no path is known yet, it discovers the workflow from Jira first, by sampling tickets, and saves it to the workspace cache. The answer names the status the ticket came from and every transition taken. A move that stops partway says where the ticket landed and is never retried. The same move within a minute is skipped.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Moves one Jira ticket to a target status, in one transition or along several when the workflow needs them.

targetStatus.description: The status to move the ticket to, e.g. "In Review" or "Done".

resolution.description: The resolution to set when the last step asks for one, e.g. "Fixed".

languageModelTools.name: jira_create_ticket
languageModelTools.displayName: Create a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Creates one Jira ticket. For a ticket the user asks for in their own words, follow the ts-jira-create skill first: it picks a template and shows the user a draft. Prefer a templateName from jira_list_templates: the template gives the issue type and default fields. Without a template, give the issueType; the issue type is never guessed, so a call without either lists the project's issue types and creates nothing. Write the description as Markdown. The answer names the template fields applied. The same ticket requested again within a minute is skipped.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Creates one Jira ticket.

templateName.description: A template name from jira_list_templates; its issue type and fields are applied.

issueType.description: The issue type, e.g. Bug. Needed when no template gives one.

description.description: The description, written as Markdown; it is converted to Jira wiki markup.

languageModelTools.name: jira_add_comment
languageModelTools.displayName: Add a comment to a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds one comment to a Jira ticket. Write the comment as Markdown (headings, lists, tables, code); it reaches Jira as wiki markup, as from @jira. The same comment on the same ticket within a minute is skipped, so a repeated call does not post it twice.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Adds one comment to a Jira ticket.

comment.description: The comment text, written as Markdown; it is converted to Jira wiki markup.

languageModelTools.name: jira_update_field
languageModelTools.displayName: Update a field of a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sets one field of one Jira ticket, named by display name or id: summary, description, priority, assignee, labels, components, fix version, sprint, or any other field such as a custom field. For a list field, operation "add" or "remove" changes single values and keeps the rest. When you do not know a field's name, look it up with jira_list_fields. To set a field on several tickets, call jira_open_board with board ticket-list and the change as change; do not call this once per ticket. The description is written as Markdown. The answer quotes the value the field had before. The same change to the same field within a minute is skipped, so a repeated call does not write it twice.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Sets one field of one Jira ticket, named by display name or id.

fieldName.description: The field, by display name or id: summary, description, priority, assignee, labels, components, fix version, sprint, or any other field such as a custom field.

value.description: The new value. The description is written as Markdown and converted to Jira wiki markup; labels and components are comma-separated; assignee is a name, an email or "me"; a sprint by its name.

operation.description: For a list field such as labels or components: add or remove the given values and keep the others. Default: set, which replaces the whole value.

languageModelTools.name: jira_correct_description
languageModelTools.displayName: Correct the description of a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Applies spelling and grammar corrections the user approved to one ticket's description, and changes nothing else: formatting, tables, code, links and mentions stay exactly as they are. Read the ticket with jira_view_ticket first and show the user the numbered corrections before calling this. Each correction must match exactly once and must not be inside code, monospace, a link target or a web address; if any correction does not fit, nothing is written and the answer names each one that did not fit. The same corrections to the same ticket within a minute are skipped.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Applies spelling and grammar corrections the user approved to one ticket's description, and changes nothing else.

before.description: The text to replace: the shortest plain-text fragment that is unique in the description, e.g. the misspelled word and the word next to it. Never across bold, italic or other formatting.

corrections.description: The corrections the user approved, in the order they were shown.

languageModelTools.name: jira_upload_attachment
languageModelTools.displayName: Upload a file to a Jira ticket
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Attaches one file from an open workspace folder to a Jira ticket. Files outside the workspace folders, in a dotfile or dotfolder (after following symlinks) or over 25 MB are refused. The same file uploaded to the same ticket within a minute is skipped.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Attaches one file from an open workspace folder to a Jira ticket.

filePath.description: The file to upload: absolute, or relative to the first workspace folder.

languageModelTools.name: jira_list_fields
languageModelTools.displayName: List the fields of a Jira ticket or issue type
languageModelTools.modelDescription: With ticketKey: lists every field of that ticket with its name, id and current value, custom fields included. With projectKey and issueType instead: lists the fields that issue type can take when a ticket is created, with name, id and whether Jira requires each. Use it to find a field's name or id for jira_update_field, a template or the display settings. Changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: With ticketKey.

ticketKey.description: A ticket key, e.g. PROJ-123: lists every field of that ticket with its current value.

projectKey.description: Without a ticket: the project key, e.g. PROJ.

issueType.description: Without a ticket: the issue type, e.g. Bug. Lists the fields that type can take on create.

languageModelTools.name: jira_check_required_fields
languageModelTools.displayName: Check a Jira ticket for the required fields
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks whether a ticket has a value in every field listed in the ticketSidekick.jira.requiredFields setting and names the empty ones. These are the fields the user's team requires, not the ones Jira enforces. Changes nothing.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Checks whether a ticket has a value in every field listed in the ticketSidekick.jira.requiredFields setting and names the empty ones.

languageModelTools.name: jira_open_board
languageModelTools.displayName: Open a Ticket Sidekick board
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Opens a board in its own editor tab: the security report of a project, a ticket list for a JQL query or saved filter, or the stored sessions. Use it whenever the user asks to see a list of tickets, to search Jira, to change more than one ticket, or for the security report; do not list the tickets in chat and do not change them one by one. For a change to several tickets, pass it as change: the user reviews and applies it on the board. The answer says only whether the board opened, never its content. Changes nothing in Jira.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Opens a board in its own editor tab.

board.description: security-report: a project's open Veracode and Waltz tickets by release. ticket-list: the tickets of a JQL query or saved filter, where the user selects tickets and moves them or sets a field. sessions: the stored board sessions of this workspace.

project.description: security-report: the Jira project key, e.g. PROJ. Leave out to use the default project.

jql.description: ticket-list: a JQL query, e.g. project = PROJ AND status = Done.

filter.description: ticket-list: a saved filter's id or name, in place of jql.

change.description: ticket-list: a change the user asked for. The board shows it as proposed and writes nothing until the user applies it.

status.description: For a transition: the status to move to.

resolution.description: For a transition: the resolution to set, if any.

field.description: For a field change: the field's name or id.

value.description: For a field change: the new value.

ticketSidekick.jira.baseUrl.description: Base URL of your Jira instance (e.g. https://jira.mycompany.com)

ticketSidekick.jira.authType.description: Jira authentication mode: 'datacenter' uses Bearer PAT, 'cloud' uses Basic email:Atlassian-apiToken

ticketSidekick.jira.defaultProject.description: Default Jira project key (e.g. 'PROJ'). Used when creating tickets if no project is specified in your prompt. Checked at start and after a change: a value that is not a project key, or a project Jira does not have, brings up a warning.

ticketSidekick.jira.overviewCsvDelimiter.description: Column separator in the CSV that the security report and the `export` reply of a report import save. Excel with a German (or other comma-decimal) locale opens a semicolon-separated file in columns, and a comma-separated one in a single column.

ticketSidekick.sessions.retentionDays.description: How many days a stored board session (a security report, list, import or review in progress) is kept after it was last used. Sessions are a cache in VS Code's storage for the workspace; `Ticket Sidekick: Clear stored sessions` deletes them all at once.

ticketSidekick.jira.sprintBoardId.description: Jira Agile board ID to use for sprint lookups. Only needed if your project has multiple Scrum boards and the wrong one is selected automatically. Find the board ID in the URL — modern Jira: .../jira/software/projects/PROJ/boards/12345 — Data Center RapidBoard: .../jira/secure/RapidBoard.jspa?rapidView=12345 (use the rapidView value).

ticketSidekick.jira.requiredFields.description: Jira field names that must be set for ticket validation (e.g. ["assignee", "priority"])

ticketSidekick.jira.showConnectionInfo.description: When enabled, each @jira response starts with an italic line showing the active base URL, API version, and auth type.

ticketSidekick.jira.additionalDisplayFie.description: Field IDs always shown in @jira show output even when their value is null. Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs (e.g. ["customfield_10020", "customfield_10500"]).

ticketSidekick.jira.searchFields.description: Field IDs to add as extra columns in @jira search results (e.g. ["priority", "customfield_10020"]). Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs.

ticketSidekick.jira.cleanupFields.description: Field IDs to add as extra columns in the @jira run cleanup / bulk transition review table (e.g. ["fixVersions", "priority"]). Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs.

ticketSidekick.jira.hiddenDisplayFields.description: Field IDs excluded from @jira show output. Fields in additionalDisplayFields override this list. Use @jira show fields on PROJ-123 to discover field IDs.

ticketSidekick.jira.myTeamJql.description: JQL fragment representing your team's tickets (e.g. 'project = BACKEND AND assignee in membersOf("backend-team")'). When you ask '@jira open tickets for my team', this is ANDed with the rest of your query.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.baseUrl.description: Base URL of your Bitbucket Data Center instance (e.g. https://bitbucket.mycompany.com). Leave empty for Bitbucket Cloud.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.authType.description: Bitbucket authentication mode: 'datacenter' uses Bearer PAT, 'cloud' uses Basic base64(username:App-password)

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.showConnectionI.description: When enabled, each @bitbucket response (except check) starts with an italic line showing the active base URL, API version, and auth type.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewInstructi.description: Additional instructions appended to the built-in PR review prompt. Use this to add project-specific guidance, e.g. 'This project follows Google Style Guide' or 'Focus on security issues only'. The built-in grounding rules and output format are always included.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.modelContextTok.description: Override the model's context window size in tokens for chunk sizing. Leave unset to use the model's reported value (recommended). Set this if auto-detection is unavailable or you want a conservative cap (e.g. 60000).

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.contextBudgetRa.description: Fraction of the model's context window a review call's prompt may use (0.1–0.9, default 0.7); review chunks are additionally capped at about 24,000 tokens so each file gets a real share of the model's answer. The rest of the window is left for the model's output. Lower this value if you see context-limit errors during reviews.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewMode.description: Default review depth, ordered by capability quick < standard < smart < deep. 'standard' enables the two-pass review where the LLM can request additional file context. 'quick' skips the second pass (diffs only) — faster and cheaper for large PRs. 'smart' adds specialist persona lenses (security, performance, reliability, maintainability) on top of standard. 'deep' adds persona lenses plus a critic (verification) pass — the most thorough and most expensive option. Override per-review with '@bitbucket review quick <url>', '@bitbucket review smart <url>', or '@bitbucket review deep <url>'.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewExcludePa.description: Glob patterns for files to skip during PR review (e.g. ["**/migrations/**", "**/*.snap", "**/*.generated.ts"]). Excluded files are not sent to the LLM; the review output notes how many were skipped.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.reviewContextLi.description: Number of unchanged context lines requested around each diff hunk (default 12). Wider context usually includes the enclosing function so the reviewer reasons about real surrounding code instead of guessing — at the cost of a larger prompt. Lower it to save tokens on large PRs.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.confidenceThres.description: Findings whose model-rated confidence falls below this value (0–1, default 0.7) show their confidence in plain instead of bold text, and a copied review marks them '(low confidence)'. They stay in their severity table and are never hidden or discarded.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.detailedDiagnos.description: When enabled, each review additionally emits a single fenced structured run record to the "Ticket Sidekick" output channel — run configuration, per-call records, and the findings funnel with drop reasons — copy-pasteable as one block for comparing runs or filing a provider bug report.

ticketSidekick.bitbucket.showTokenUsage.description: When enabled, every @bitbucket answer (review, follow-up, comment refinement) ends with one line showing its input and output tokens and the model, for example "Tokens: 41,230 in · 6,840 out · claude-sonnet-4.5". Counts come from the editor's tokenizer and are approximate (a ~ marks estimates). Usage is recorded for @bitbucket usage whether or not this is on.

ticketSidekick.email.deleteEmlAfterImpor.description: Delete the .eml file automatically after the Jira ticket is created.

ticketSidekick.email.maxBatchSizeMB.description: Maximum total size, in MB, of a selected .eml batch. Raise this if your email batch import is rejected for exceeding the size limit.

ticketSidekick.email.boilerplatePatterns.description: Known boilerplate to remove from imported emails: confidentiality headers, legal footers and signatures. Each entry has a kind (header, footer or signature), a start phrase and an optional end phrase. Phrases are plain text, not regular expressions; matching ignores case, extra spaces and bold/italic markers, and runs on every message of the thread, including quoted ones. With an end phrase, the block runs from the start phrase through the line containing the end phrase, and only matches where the end phrase follows the start phrase in the same message. Without one, a header covers the line(s) its start phrase is on (add an end phrase for multi-line headers), and a footer or signature runs until the next matched block, the next quoted message, or the end of the message, at most 40 lines. You are always shown what was found before anything is removed.

kind.description: What the block is: a header (e.g. an external-sender warning), a footer (e.g. a legal disclaimer) or a signature.

start.description: Text the block starts with, e.g. "CONFIDENTIALITY NOTICE:".

end.description: Optional text on the block's last line, e.g. "Registered office Frankfurt am Main."

ticketSidekick.veracode.minSeverity.description: Minimum Veracode severity (0=Informational … 5=Very High) to include when importing a Detailed Report. Flaws below this are filtered out by default (still visible in the raw XML).

ticketSidekick.veracode.includeRemediati.description: Veracode remediation_status values to include when importing a Detailed Report (e.g. exclude 'Fixed' or 'Mitigated'). Valid values: Cannot Reproduce, Fixed, Mitigated, New, Open, Potential False Positive, Remediated by User, Reopened, Reviewed - No Action Taken.

ticketSidekick.veracode.maxReportSizeMB.description: Maximum size, in MB, of a Veracode Detailed Report XML file. Raise this if your report is rejected for exceeding the size limit.

Very High.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for Very High flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

High.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for High flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

Medium.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for Medium flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

Low.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for Low flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

Very Low.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for Very Low flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

Informational.description: Calendar days from the first-found date to the due date for Informational flaws. 0 means no Due Date.

ticketSidekick.veracode.slaDays.description: Calendar days from the date Veracode first found a flaw to the Jira Due Date of its ticket, per severity. 0 means no Due Date for that severity. A ticket's Due Date is set once and never overwritten by a later import; flaws added to a ticket can only move it earlier.

ticketSidekick.waltz.minVulnRating.description: Minimum 'Max Vuln Rating' to include when importing an OSS report. Components rated below this are filtered out by default (still visible in the raw file).

ticketSidekick.waltz.includeRemediationA.description: Remediation Action values to include when importing an OSS report (empty string means the column was blank). Components with any other action (e.g. 'Risk capture') are excluded by default.

ticketSidekick.waltz.maxReportSizeMB.description: Maximum size, in MB, of an OSS Report .xlsx file. Raise this if your report is rejected for exceeding the size limit.

walkthroughs.title: Ticket Sidekick: Jira
walkthroughs.description: Set up @jira and create your first ticket.

steps.title: Set your Jira base URL
steps.description:
Point Ticket Sidekick at your Jira instance.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.jira.baseUrl%22)

steps.title: Add your Jira credentials
steps.description:
Store a Data Center Personal Access Token or Cloud email + API token in VS Code's encrypted Secret Storage.
[Set Data Center Token](command:ticket-sidekick.setDataCenterToken)
[Configure Cloud Credentials](command:ticket-sidekick.configureCloud)

steps.title: Set a default project
steps.description:
So `@jira create` and the report importers don't need a project key in every prompt.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.jira.defaultProject%22)

steps.title: Discover your ticket types & workflow
steps.description:
Sample your project's real tickets to learn its issue types and status-transition graph.
[Ask @jira](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20discover%20workflow%20%3CPROJECT%3E%20%3CISSUE_TYPE%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)

steps.title: Create your first ticket
steps.description:
Generate a template from real project data, then create a ticket from it — or create one directly.
[Ask @jira](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20generate%20a%20template%22%7D%5D)
[Or create directly](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40jira%20create%20%3CTYPE%3E%20in%20%3CPROJECT%3E%3A%20%3CSUMMARY%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)

steps.title: Use the Jira tools in Copilot chats
steps.description:
Copilot's agent can read and change Jira tickets through Ticket Sidekick's tools, and open boards (ticket lists, the security report) in editor tabs. Type `/ts-jira help` in a Copilot chat to see the commands.
[Open stored sessions](command:ticket-sidekick.boards.sessions)

walkthroughs.title: Ticket Sidekick: Bitbucket
walkthroughs.description: Set up @bitbucket and review your first pull request.

steps.title: Set your Bitbucket base URL (Data Center only)
steps.description:
Point Ticket Sidekick at your Bitbucket Data Center instance. Skip this on Bitbucket Cloud — Cloud always talks to the fixed api.bitbucket.org host.
[Open setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22ticketSidekick.bitbucket.baseUrl%22)

steps.title: Add your Bitbucket credentials
steps.description:
Store a Data Center Personal Access Token or Cloud username + App Password in VS Code's encrypted Secret Storage.
[Set Data Center Token](command:ticket-sidekick.setBitbucketDataCenterToken)
[Configure Cloud Credentials](command:ticket-sidekick.configureBitbucketCloud)

steps.title: Review your first pull request
steps.description:
Paste a real Bitbucket PR URL to @bitbucket and get a structured, line-accurate review.
[Ask @bitbucket](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40bitbucket%20check%22%7D%5D)
[Review a PR](command:workbench.action.chat.open?%5B%7B%22query%22%3A%22%40bitbucket%20%3CURL%3E%22%2C%22isPartialQuery%22%3Atrue%7D%5D)
